concept.name: Daily review
concept.definition: An end-of-day routine in which the day's trades are logged, graded against plan rules, and analyzed for errors and lessons before the next session. It is the shortest feedback loop in the trading process and the primary driver of incremental improvement.
concept.intuition: Ten honest minutes with the day's trades each evening is worth more than ten hours of new course material.
concept.mechanics: Typical steps: reconcile fills, tag each trade by setup, score rule adherence, classify errors (analysis, execution, risk), note emotional state, and write one or two actionable lessons; results feed the weekly review. Professional prop desks institutionalize recorded daily trade review.
concept.failure_modes: It is skipped on losing days - when it matters most - or degrades into P&L checking, losing its function. The opposite failure is overreacting to a single day's noise by rewriting rules nightly.
concept.misconceptions: Daily review is not about judging the day's profit; one day is almost pure variance. It is also not optional maintenance - it is where plan, journal, and psychology connect.
concept.example: After the close a trader replays his three trades, tags one as a C-setup he should not have taken, notes he hesitated on a valid entry, and writes both into tomorrow's pre-market notes.

citations.source: Mike Bellafiore, One Good Trade: Inside the Highly Competitive World of Proprietary Trading (Wiley, 2010) - publisher page
